standard_prerequisites.use: Describes g_{n!}G as the module whose degree m part is the direct sum of f_phi^*G, and the assumptions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flat pullback exactness
standard_prerequisites.use: If f_phi^{-1}O_n -> O_m are flat then f_phi^* is exact.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1532-1539): under the hypotheses of the restriction lemma, the functor g_{n!} : Mod(O_n) -> Mod(O) is exact provided the maps f_phi^{-1}O_n -> O_m are flat for all phi : [n] -> [m].

Degree description (proof lines 1541-1548): g_{n!}G is the O-module whose degree m part is the O_m-module direct sum over phi : [n] -> [m] of f_phi^*G, where f_phi is the morphism of ringed topoi built from the ring map of the statement.

Conclusion (lines 1548-1556): if the ring maps are flat then each f_phi^* is exact (Modules on Sites lemma), so by the definition of the site C_total these functors have the desired exactness properties; the functor g_{n!} is exact.
proof_roadmap: Write the degree-m part of g_{n!}G as a direct sum of flat pullbacks.
Use flatness to get exactness of each f_phi^*.
Conclude exactness of g_{n!} from the site definition.
difficulty_reason: Exactness lemma (statement 1532-1539, proof 1541-1556): exactness of the lower shriek functor under flat ring maps - the proof computes the degree parts as direct sums of pullbacks and transports exactness componentwise through the flat-pullback lemma; short but complete. H3.
